    Version History

Mozilla announced the release of version 0.12 of the Rust compiler and tools in October 2014.

Version 0.12 included over 1,900 changes and bug fixes, which mainly involved: rewriting the introductory documentation (now called The Rust Guide); and further improving the package manager Cargo, among others.

In January 2015, Rust-1.0.0-alpha was released.

On May 15, 2015, the Rust programming language core team officially announced the release of Rust version 1.0. [...] "Rust" was initially a personal project by Graydon Hoare of Mozilla. In 2009, Mozilla began sponsoring the project, with several Mozilla employees participating in the design and development of the Rust language. In August 2013, Graydon Hoare stepped down from his role as technical lead for Rust, and Brian Anderson took over. On May 15, 2015, the Rust 1.0 version was officially released. In September 2017, Brian Anderson left Mozilla, and the project's core team was taken over and co-led by [...] the first compiler with a version number was released in January 2012. The 1.0 stable version was officially released on May 15, 2015, version 1.90.0 was released on September 18, 2025, and the current version is 1.91.0. In August 2013, Graydon Hoare stepped down from the technical lead position, succeeded by Brian Anderson; after September 2017, the core team was co-led by Aaron Turon and Niko Matsakis.
